::: {.callout-note}
## About this page

This page **tests the panzoom extension** with the knitr graphics devices
used in practice: webp, svg and pdf output, for a wide collage and a
standard plot. Every figure is marked with `#| panzoom: true` and should
open the pan/zoom viewer, except where a case says otherwise. Figure
shapes and how they open are on [H: wide and tall figures](h-wide.html).

Headings carry what the browser test checks: `expect-fit` (the opening
view: `contain`, `height` or `width`), `shift-scroll` (which way
Shift+scroll moves the image: `x`, `y` or `none`) and `expect-scale="1"`
(opens at real size, not enlarged).

webp comes from ragg's `agg_webp` device: knitr has no built-in webp
device, and `agg_webp` needs `units = "in"` because knitr passes sizes in
inches.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false

library(ragg)

# A collage: `n` panels side by side, like a wide patchwork figure.
collage <- function(n = 12) {
  set.seed(1)
  par(mfrow = c(1, n), mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1))
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    plot(cumsum(rnorm(200)), type = "l", main = paste("Panel", i),
         xlab = "", ylab = "", col = hcl.colors(n)[i], lwd = 2)
  }
}
```

## 1. Wide collage, webp (25 × 2 in) {#c1 expect-fit="height"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 96)
#| fig-cap: "A 25 × 2 inch collage of 12 panels (webp)."

collage()
```

## 2. Wide collage, svg (25 × 2 in) {#c2 expect-fit="height"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 25
#| fig-height: 2
#| dev: svg
#| fig-cap: "The collage as svg."

collage()
```

## 3. webp plot {#c3 expect-fit="contain" shift-scroll="none" expect-scale="1"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 96)
#| fig-cap: "A standard-size plot as webp."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 4. svg plot {#c4 expect-fit="contain" expect-scale="1"}

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: svg
#| fig-cap: "A standard-size plot as svg."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 5. png + pdf (dev: [png, pdf]) {#c5 expect-fit="contain"}

Both files are written; the page shows the png.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: !expr c("png", "pdf")
#| fig-cap: "png shown, pdf written alongside."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 6. pdf only {#c6}

With only the pdf device, the HTML page has no bitmap to show; this case
records what the browser and panzoom do with it.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: pdf
#| fig-cap: "pdf only."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors)
```

## 7. png + cairo_pdf (dev: [png, cairo_pdf]) {#c7 expect-fit="contain"}

Like case 5, with the cairo PDF device, which embeds fonts and handles
Unicode (µ, Greek letters) and transparency better than `pdf`. The page
shows the png either way; a PDF figure only ever appears as the browser's
PDF viewer (case 6), whichever device wrote it.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| dev: !expr c("png", "cairo_pdf")
#| fig-cap: "png shown, cairo_pdf written alongside (mu = 5, alpha = 0.05)."

filled.contour(volcano, color.palette = terrain.colors,
               plot.title = title(main = "mu = 5, alpha = 0.05"))
```

## 8. Wide collage, webp at 2× resolution (100 × 5 in) {#c8}

At 192 dpi the collage is 19,200 px wide, beyond webp's limit of 16,383 px
per side; this case records what happens.

```{r}
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-width: 100
#| fig-height: 5
#| dev: agg_webp
#| fig-ext: webp
#| dev.args: !expr list(units = "in", res = 192)
#| fig-cap: "The collage as webp at 192 dpi."
#| error: true

collage()
```
